title: add benchmark-lab kernel-selection profiling runners and reporting pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: kernel selection has a measurable impact on latency and throughput for varying sequence lengths and quantization profiles. This PR adds a set of benchmark-lab workload runners that capture kernel selection traces (kernel id + invocation counts + timing), expands profiling baselines to include kernel-level summaries, and wires those artifacts into the existing reporting pipeline so dashboards can show kernel usage by model variant and sequence-length buckets. What this changes: 1) new workload runners (python) that emit kernel_trace.json alongside existing perf artifacts; 2) profiler baseline generation scripts that aggregate kernel metrics into a canonical baseline CSV; 3) reporting pipeline changes to ingest kernel_trace.json, normalize kernel ids across hardware families, and surface kernel-level graphs in the performance dashboard; 4) small runtime shim to tag requests with the model_variant and quantization_profile. Checklist: - [x] workload runners implemented and unit-tested - [x] baseline generator implemented and smoke-tested locally - [x] reporting pipeline consumers added and end-to-end smoke verified on staging - [x] docs updated (benchmark-lab README + reporting README) - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-9421, ENG-9477). Notes: this is additive instrumentation only and does not change production runtime kernels or schedules. Follow-ups planned to correlate kernel selection to tail latency (ENG-9522).
